purpose: Compare Divine Pattern findings with major Christian thinkers throughout church history for theological grounding, not automatic agreement.

records.name: Irenaeus
records.agreements: Supports Christ as the one who recapitulates and restores creation.
records.disagreements: Requires guarding the project from speculative systems detached from apostolic teaching.

records.name: Justin Martyr
records.agreements: Supports careful engagement with philosophy under Christ the Logos.
records.disagreements: Philosophical parallels must remain subordinate to revelation in Christ.

records.name: Athanasius
records.agreements: Supports the claim that creation and restoration are interpreted through the incarnate Son.
records.disagreements: The project must preserve Nicene Christology and avoid reducing Christ to a pattern symbol.

records.name: Augustine
records.agreements: Supports distortion through disordered love and restoration through grace.
records.disagreements: Warns against trusting human observation without grace and illumination.

records.name: Thomas Aquinas
records.agreements: Supports ordered creation and reason while distinguishing nature and grace.
records.disagreements: Requires careful limits on analogy and strong distinction between creature and Creator.

records.name: Martin Luther
records.agreements: Supports centering grace and the cross over human moral achievement.
records.disagreements: Challenges any version of the project that makes patterns into a ladder to God.

records.name: John Calvin
records.agreements: Supports Scripture's authority, providence, and serious doctrine of sin.
records.disagreements: Warns that fallen perception can turn creation patterns into idolatry.

records.name: C.S. Lewis
records.agreements: Supports moral law, longing, and imagination as pointers when tested by Christian revelation.
records.disagreements: Longing and imagination are signs, not independent authorities.

records.name: G.K. Chesterton
records.agreements: Supports wonder, paradox, and gratitude as Christian responses to creation.
records.disagreements: Poetic pattern recognition still needs doctrinal discipline.

records.name: Basil of Caesarea
records.agreements: Supports Nicene trinitarian grammar and practical care for vulnerable people as theological fruit.
records.disagreements: Pattern language must not replace doctrinal precision about Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

records.name: Maximus the Confessor
records.agreements: Supports creation as ordered toward Christ while preserving Christological depth.
records.disagreements: The project must avoid reducing participation in God to generic self-improvement or cosmic symbolism.

records.name: Teresa of Avila
records.agreements: Supports transformation as grace-shaped communion rather than technique or performance.
records.disagreements: Mystical pattern language must remain accountable to humility, obedience, and discernment.

records.name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
records.agreements: Supports grace as costly transformation and Christian witness under political pressure.
records.disagreements: The project must resist abstract pattern claims that avoid obedience, risk, and public truth.

records.name: James H. Cone
records.agreements: Pressures the project to connect the cross with real histories of racial terror, liberation, and truth-telling.
records.disagreements: Any divine-pattern claim that ignores racialized suffering or treats justice as optional should be weakened.
citations: The Cross and the Lynching Tree

records.name: Emmanuel Katongole
records.agreements: Supports hope and reconciliation only when lament, history, violence, and political reality remain visible.
records.disagreements: The project must not turn reconciliation into a slogan that bypasses grief, truth, and costly repair.
